{"ts":"git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Add opt-in --phylogenetics stage: MAFFT + IQ-TREE reassortment analysis

Extracts CDS nucleotide sequences for human-affecting-or-likely,
divergence-candidate, and complete-triplet isolates, aligns each species'
S/M/L segments with MAFFT, builds ML trees with IQ-TREE (ModelFinder +
ultrafast bootstrap), and replaces the withdrawn k-mer reassortment
classifier with real tree-distance diagnostics, bootstrap-gated
reassortment calls, and Robinson-Foulds topology comparison. Writes
ortho_reassortment_table.parquet, gated behind --phylogenetics so the
default pipeline is unaffected.

Validated end-to-end on the full dataset: 1,464 candidate isolates across
14 species (up to 424 taxa), no failures, 1,445 no_conflict / 2
weak_signal_low_bootstrap_support / 0 supported_reassortment_candidate.

Also fixes two review-confirmed correctness bugs found after that run:
the --phylogenetics block ran before the core "Writing outputs" section,
so any failure in the opt-in stage (missing mafft/iqtree, a bad tree)
would abort the whole run before a single core table was written; and
_analyze_species only wrapped the MAFFT/IQ-TREE subprocess calls in
try/except, not the downstream tree-parsing/RF code, so a failure there
escaped the per-species error isolation the docstring claimed. Both are
now fixed and verified: a simulated missing-binary failure still writes
all 12 core output tables with exit code 0. Also fixed a cosmetic bug
where below-threshold species rows always recorded n_taxa_in_species_tree
as 0 instead of the actual candidate count.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)""}

{"ts":"git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Flag lab-derived isolates in the ML matrix instead of filtering them

build_ml_tables previously excluded every is_lab_derived isolate, using the
same rationale --phylogenetics uses for excluding them from tree-building.
But NCBI's isLabHost field marks the immediate recorded host, not sequence
contamination: of 164 is_lab_derived isolates, 21 have host_taxid 9606 --
lab-acquired/occupational human infections concentrated in the highest-CFR
species (HTNV, ANDV, PUUV, DOBV) -- and most of the rest are samples from
colony-maintained reservoir animals, not culture-adapted sequences.
Blanket-filtering them discarded real positive evidence of human/reservoir
infection for a pathogenicity-prediction task; a study comparing
human-derived and reservoir Orthohantavirus sequences for zoonotic-risk
assessment found the human sequences are themselves the spillover-risk
baseline, not noise to remove
(https://microbiomejournal.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s40168-025-02059-0).

is_lab_derived isolates are now kept and exposed as an explicit
is_lab_derived column so a model can be trained/compared with or without
them. is_vaccine_strain isolates (2) remain excluded: deliberate
attenuation would inject a real label error, not a hypothetical one.

--phylogenetics is unaffected: it keeps excluding both is_lab_derived and
is_vaccine_strain, since passage/attenuation history is a tree-topology
risk (branch-length distortion) independent of whether a sequence is
informative as an ML feature. Verified: default pipeline counts unchanged
(15,991/39/9,852/223), --phylogenetics candidate selection unchanged
(1,464/17 split), ML feature matrix grows 7,498 -> 7,651 rows (+153
lab-derived isolates, 21 of them real human infections).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)""}

## Digest: Session `de97c6fc` (Orthohantavirus pipeline)

**Date range:** 2026-07-30 14:38 UTC → 2026-07-31 15:59 UTC (~25.5 hours elapsed, including a long unattended overnight background run).

### Chronological thread

**1. Protein-count discrepancy (07-30, ~14:45–15:07 UTC)**
User asked why `ortho_pipeline.log` reported 15,504 protein sequences vs. 15,568 shown on NCBI Virus. Assistant explained it as a query-scope difference (NCBI Datasets CLI package vs. NCBI Virus web filter), not a pipeline bug, and confirmed no action was needed since the pipeline was already up to date. No code changed.

**2. Project-aims review (07-30, 16:20–17:12 UTC)**
User asked for a full aims audit ("what's done, what's missing, is IQ-TREE/MAFFT necessary") and had the assistant re-read the whole repo for accuracy. Aim 1 (NCBI metadata collection) and Aim 2 (pathogenicity classification) were judged solid — but Aim 2 was "labeled, not filtered" (deliberate design). Aim 3 (real reassortment detection) was flagged as unmet — the existing k-mer-based classifier had been withdrawn/was inadequate — and MAFFT/IQ-TREE were judged necessary to do it properly. Aim 4 (ML training/prediction) was flagged as scaffolding only — no actual model training code existed.

**3. Phylogenetics stage build — `check/reassortment` branch**
User directed extraction of human-affecting/divergence-candidate/complete-triplet isolates for MAFFT+IQ-TREE analysis on a new branch (`check/reassortment` — created in the portion of this session that was later auto-compacted, so its exact `git checkout -b` isn't visible in the raw log, but is confirmed via `git log`/`git diff` against `main`). Delivered: a new opt-in `--phylogenetics` CLI stage in `all_hanta.py` (~550 lines) that parses `cds.fna` into a segment-aware CDS index (handling 134 multi-CDS accessions), selects candidates as the union of the three named groups (excluding lab/vaccine isolates), runs MAFFT alignment + IQ-TREE ML trees per segment/species (ModelFinder, ultrafast bootstrap, fixed seed), and derives real patristic-distance and Robinson-Foulds diagnostics replacing the withdrawn k-mer classifier — writing `output/ortho_reassortment_table.parquet`.

**4. Background full-dataset run (job `bd2hq50u8`), 07-30 ~19:00 → 07-31 ~11:00**
User asked for repeated progress checks every 20–30 min (dozens of check-ins logged, including one stretch where the sandbox itself was suspended for hours — not IQ-TREE hanging). A cron-style loop (`acf8ca80`, firing every 25 min) was set up to auto-resume checking. Mid-run, user asked for a "bulletized" description of candidate-selection logic to cross-check against "only human-affecting-or-potential" species — this surfaced that 4 of 14 species (CBNV, DBSV, JJUV, KHAV) had no human-disease label but were pulled in only via `complete_triplet`/`divergence_candidate`; a scope fix was applied and verified to reproduce identical counts for the 10 truly human-affecting species. Run completed successfully: **1,464 candidate isolates across 14 species (up to 424 taxa for PUUV), 1,447 analyzed / 17 below-taxa-threshold, reassortment calls: 1,445 no_conflict / 2 weak_signal_low_bootstrap_support / 0 supported_reassortment_candidate** — no strong reassortment signal found (itself treated as a legitimate result).

**5. Post-run pipeline: `/simplify` → `/code-review` → fix → commit (pre-authorized by user at 21:52 07-30)**
`/simplify` ran 4 parallel review agents (reuse/simplify/efficiency/altitude), fixes applied, no regression. `/code-review` spawned 11 sub-agents and found a real bug (fixed). Two additional correctness bugs were caught and fixed: (a) the `--phylogenetics` block ran *before* core output writing, so a phylo failure would abort the whole run before core tables were written; (b) `_analyze_species` only wrapped MAFFT/IQ-TREE subprocess calls in try/except, not downstream tree-parsing/RF code, breaking per-species error isolation. Also fixed a cosmetic bug where below-threshold species always recorded `n_taxa_in_species_tree` as 0. **Committed** on `check/reassortment`: "Add opt-in --phylogenetics stage: MAFFT + IQ-TREE reassortment analysis" (scoped to `all_hanta.py`, `README.md`, `ortho_reassortment_table.parquet`, `ortho_summary.json` — intermediate alignments/trees deliberately excluded per user instruction).

**6. Lab-strain ML flagging fix — new branch `ml-lab-strain-flagging`**
User cited a paper (springer/microbiomejournal link) suggesting lab strains can help ML training if validated, and chose the "flag, don't filter" option on a fresh branch off `check/reassortment` to avoid disturbing prior results. Root issue: `build_ml_tables` was blanket-excluding all `is_lab_derived` isolates (164 total), but 21 of those have `host_taxid 9606` — real occupational human infections concentrated in HTNV/ANDV/SEOV/PUUV/DOBV, the highest-CFR species — discarding positive pathogenicity evidence. Fix: only `is_vaccine_strain` (2 isolates) is now hard-excluded; `is_lab_derived` isolates are kept with a new explicit `is_lab_derived` column. `--phylogenetics` candidate selection deliberately left untouched (passage history is a tree-topology risk independent of ML usefulness). Verified: default pipeline unchanged (15,991/39/9,852/223 counts, ~15s runtime); `ortho_ml_feature_matrix.parquet` grew 7,498 → 7,651 rows. Two commits: `d5f5a51` (code+README) and `7de7679` (regenerated outputs, scaling stats).

**7. Branch hygiene and push**
User wanted `main` left intact. Verified local `main` == `origin/main` (`c42efd5`), nothing had leaked in. Pushed `check/reassortment` (→`7c14cd4`) and `ml-lab-strain-flagging` (→`7de7679`) as new remote branches; `main` untouched on GitHub.

**8. Final deliverable: published report artifact**
User requested a "complete and tidy report... for a passionate but dumb PhD student" explaining all branches and the scoring methodology. Assistant built and published an HTML artifact ("The Orthohantavirus Pipeline — Field Report") covering: branch map/lineage, `main`'s `surveillance_priority_score` formula with two worked numeric examples (HTNV human case = 5.5, TULV wild case = 1.0), the `check/reassortment` MAFFT/IQ-TREE methodology and results, the `ml-lab-strain-flagging` fix rationale, and an explicit "what's still missing" section stating the actual novel-virus prediction/ML model (Aim 4) has not been built — only its data foundation exists.

Both feature branches (`check/reassortment`, `ml-lab-strain-flagging`) are committed, pushed, and clean; `main` is untouched. The open gap going into "next steps" is Aim 4: no training code, no train/test split, no similarity-scoring/prediction model exists yet — that's the natural next task for the coordinator to raise.
